limitations: Neither participant is independent of the final artifact as a whole.

Independence applies only to the opposite participant's listed change scope. Review-edge scopes are the journal's canonical work units and participant summaries are checked against them, but scope labels and author/reviewer assignments remain attestations rather than mechanically derived facts.
The schema-v2 journal and validator were implemented by Codex in response to Claude's finding; their structure is test-covered but the review infrastructure itself has no third-party reviewer.

findings.issue: The archive-derived prose claimed that USDT/KRX had never existed in legacy and that fallback always left three bank rows. The pinned code proves only the current allowlist, while iOS visibility can leave fewer than three rows and investing is not a bank.
findings.disposition: Scoped the claim to the pinned legacy source set and replaced the fixed row count with the actual investing/kb/hana overlap subject to user visibility. The frozen archive remains unchanged as provenance, not as a truth source.

findings.issue: The document promoted an uncommitted project.pbxproj observation to a current canonical fact even though the frozen baseline explicitly excludes that worktree state.
findings.disposition: Removed the volatile one-change assertion. The document now states only the pinned Release default, records the zero-result pinned project-file grep, and keeps arming as a user-owned explicit-GO gate.

findings.issue: Baseline B1 is explicitly limited to two publisher modules, but the output stated a server-wide absence of periodic republishing without auditing callers.
findings.disposition: Preserved B1's scope and audited the external scheduler path. broadcast_rates_once wakes periodically, but topic publication is inside the payload-is_changed branch, so the supported conclusion is absence of an unconditional data-plane heartbeat or republish contract.

findings.issue: Several multi-claim units had a real citation that supported only the first clause, allowing the remaining operational assertion to borrow unrelated provenance.
findings.disposition: Added the missing pinned lines for Date()-based graph ingestion, current-rate/validRange flow, existing B1/B4 tests, post-ACK snapshot order, dormant AST tripwire, and the full auth_executor resource-bound warning.

findings.issue: The conservative claim lint omitted current-code assertions that lacked its exact cue/verb shape, so a green 55-entry ledger was not an exhaustive semantic review.
findings.disposition: Performed a broader reverse audit of every logical unit and all 86 output requirements, added local baseline or pinned file-line evidence, and regenerated the ledger at 59 explicitly reviewed candidates.

findings.issue: The cutover inventory said GraphViewModel had no consuming View and grouped its runtime object with zero-use symbols. RootView still consumes it for stop(), and the object installs callbacks and observers even though the legacy graph UI is not mounted.
findings.disposition: Separated zero-call symbols from the live GraphViewModel object and expanded the removal scope to callback, observer, environment, and stop wiring while preserving the no-production-start conclusion.

findings.issue: The first C2 draft kept an unconditional anonymous-subscribe statement and cited only the first line of each new stage layer. Those locators did not establish the enum/default, filter result, dispatcher registration, production injection, unsubscribe behavior, or pre-flag observation ordering.
findings.disposition: Rewrote the anonymous path as stage-dependent and cited complete pinned ranges for config, rollout policy, dispatcher application, production injection, unsubscribe, and metric ordering. The documents now distinguish the code default from the unmeasured operating stage and keep the premium/USDT gap open.

findings.issue: Moving pinned source lines and changing the anonymous-stage prose invalidated reviewed-unit hashes. Treating all drift as mechanical would have carried the obsolete unconditional-anonymous detail into the new claims.
findings.disposition: Carried forward only nine byte-identical classifications, reviewed the changed premium-gap and stage units independently, and regenerated an exact 60-entry ledger with 48 code facts and 12 normative units.

findings.issue: After Codex modified the final C2 documents and ledger, retaining a single 'independent semantic reviewer' attribution made Codex both co-author and global reviewer. The hashes were valid, but the independence claim was not.
findings.disposition: Replaced the global-independence claim with schema-v2 reciprocal cross-review. The journal records two non-self review edges, explicitly states that no participant is independent of the whole artifact, and the validator rejects self-review, one-way review, and false global-independence controls.

findings.issue: The first schema-v2 validator checked non-self review edges and exact duplicate prose, but did not bind participant authored/reviewed summaries to edge scopes. Reworded self-review or unrelated participant scopes therefore passed while the edges remained unchanged.
findings.disposition: Made review-edge scopes the canonical work units, required participant summaries to equal the scopes derived from their outgoing and incoming edges, rejected scope reuse across edges, and added adversarial controls for reworded self-review, participant/edge disagreement, and reused scopes. Scope labels and author/reviewer assignments remain explicitly attested rather than mechanically proven.

findings.issue: send_initial_snapshots built and sent payloads directly after subscription registration without rechecking the shared lease gate, even though leased_subscribers documents itself as the single gate shared by every publish path. A lease could expire, or the registry entry could disappear, while the snapshot builder ran in to_thread outside the authentication wire deadline, and the initial snapshot would still be sent. The defect escaped because the structural guards covered dispatcher publish functions but not the initial-snapshot module, and because the original unit tests invoked send_initial_snapshots with no registry state and therefore could not express lease eligibility at all.
findings.disposition: Commit 882d92b reuses leased_subscribers after each snapshot build and immediately before send_json. Leaseless E1 subscriptions still receive snapshots, only the ineligible topic is skipped, and five regression tests cover a valid lease, an expired lease, a leaseless subscription, registry disappearance during build, and skip-versus-abort. A naive registry.get_lease() check was rejected because its None conflates leaseless subscription with vanished registration. The reviewer inspected the implementation and call paths and independently ran the 33 direct unit tests; the author's three mutation controls were reviewed as reported but were not independently rerun by the reviewer.

findings.issue: The first S2a re-baseline attempt updated the baseline facts but left two current-code locators in the generated handoff document pointing at pre-882d92b line numbers. The author classified them as frozen archive quotations and declined to touch them; that classification was wrong. The archive line carries no locator at all, so both ranges are current-code claims owned by the generated document, and the claim ledger had copied one of them as a code_fact. Nothing in the hash chain detects this: every hash stayed internally consistent while the locators pointed at the wrong lines.
findings.disposition: Both ranges were remapped from the pre-commit file by content with function-scope disambiguation (275-296 to 277-307, 275-286 to 277-297) and the affected claim-ledger unit was regenerated from the validator's own candidate extractor rather than edited by hand. The reviewer identified one of the two stale ranges; the author found the second while remapping. The residual limit stands: locator correctness inside generated documents is not mechanically verified, only hash consistency is.

residual_limits: Natural-language completeness and citation entailment are not mechanically provable; this journal records reciprocal human-model cross-review bound to exact output hashes.
Negative repository facts use full-tree searches at the pinned commits and must be rerun if either pinned commit changes.
The documents remain Draft implementation contracts. Passing this review confirms the cited C1 code path at the pinned commit, not operating activation or completion of R-GATE-1.
The current operating WS_TOPIC_AUTH_STAGE and production flag values were not measured; they remain direct-measurement gates before activation.
The 2026-08-12 historical amendment before ADR-041 is outside the document hash used by this journal and remains a separately reviewed, non-hash-bound note.
Release arming remains excluded from the frozen baseline and requires a separate explicit GO.
The initial-snapshot lease gate authorizes the start of send_json, not its completion; an in-flight send may finish after the lease expires.
A post-ACK snapshot skip is fail-closed but produces no removal, reauthorization, or close notification, so a client can be told a topic was accepted and then receive no initial data.

The shared lease gate performs an O(number of subscribers) scan and set allocation per topic. This is accepted for the current scale and supported-topic bound, not established as a large-scale guarantee.

Code locators inside generated documents are not mechanically checked against the code they name; the hash chain only proves internal consistency, so a stale locator can survive a fully green re-baseline (SEM-012).
